population.note: FICTIONAL. Ever 30.5% − current 21.4% = 9.1% of adults have used and are off now. The 4.0 pts of new ever-users since 2030 split into 3.0 on and 1.0 already off. Of the 26.5 pts who had used by 2030, 18.4 are on and 8.1 are off. On: 3.0 + 18.4 = 21.4. Off: 1.0 + 8.1 = 9.1. Within the 2030 cohort, 10.5 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (56%, up from ~50% because monthly MariTide and clinic-administered dosing lift persistence). The other 8.3 stopped and joined the 7.7 already off, a pool of 16.0. Of that pool 7.9 restarted (49%, below 2030's 55% because the pool now holds more deliberate opt-outs). 10.5 + 7.9 = 18.4, and 16.0 − 7.9 = 8.1. Cycled: the 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030 plus ~3.4 pts of first-time restarts = 12.3 of 30.5 ever-users = 40%. New ever-users are fewer than in 2028–30 because flat HRSA funding, stalled prices and no new state programme slowed entry. Most of the new entrants are normal-BMI 'metabolic healthspan' users in the top third (top 25→29). Adults ≈268M, so current users ≈57.4M. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23% give 2.60 + 7.76 + 7.92 + 3.11 = 21.4. Income thirds (29 + 21 + 14.2)/3 = 21.4. The bottom third rose only 1.2 pts because the HRSA programme was flat-funded with waitlists. The marginal low-income entrant is a gray-market or imported-pen user. Off-drug: ~24.4M adults who used and stopped, plus ~186M who never used. Pediatric: ~1.0% of ~73M ≈ 730k under-18s, of whom ≈130k are aged 6–11, nearly all on generic liraglutide from FQHCs. The oldest adolescent cohorts have ~9 years of exposure, and the first interim registry bone data (2032) are ambiguous.

access.public_coverage: Structure unchanged. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was extended in the Dec 2031 extenders package on identical terms ($275/month payment, $50 copay, DEXA counselling for 65+) through 2033. About 2.6M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 2.6M × $275 × 12 ≈ $8.6B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈15.5% of fills ≈ 8.9M users (≈7.9M aged 65+ plus ≈1.0M disabled under-65; the remaining ~0.4M 65+ users pay cash or buy gray). Medicaid pays ≈10.5% ≈ 6.0M users at $275: 6.0M × $275 × 12 ≈ $19.8B/yr combined. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged, and the three pending state applications were neither approved nor withdrawn. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program is flat-funded at $4.5B by full-year continuing resolutions for FY2031 and FY2032, with no new appropriation language. It still serves ≈3.0M: 2.0M liraglutide × $85 × 12 = $2.04B, plus 1.0M semaglutide × $199 × 12 = $2.39B, ≈ $4.43B. FQHC waitlists average 7–10 weeks in high-demand states. MariTide is not in the Bridge; Amgen declined the $275 rate.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month, and generic tirzepatide launched in Indian and Brazilian markets in 2031 at $25–60/month. Mexico, Canada, Turkey and China sell generic semaglutide, and Chinese API supply roughly doubled. Generic oral semaglutide is sold in ~180 countries. In the US, Paragraph IV settlements (Feb 2031) set generic semaglutide entry no earlier than Apr 2033. Tirzepatide exclusivity runs well past that.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ≈57.4M users: commercial 35% (20.1M), Medicare 15.5% (8.9M), Medicaid 10.5% (6.0M), HRSA free 5.2% (3.0M), cash/direct 14.3% (8.2M), gray 19.5% (11.2M); 20.1 + 8.9 + 6.0 + 3.0 + 8.2 + 11.2 = 57.4. No structural change in who pays: gray grew by 1.5 pts of share and HRSA shrank by 0.8 pts of share at a flat count. Prices stalled. TrumpRx/direct cash stays at $349 (semaglutide), $449 (tirzepatide) and $199 (oral start). The Section 232 tariff stands. Wegovy lists at $1,349 and retatrutide at $1,499, still allocated with no cash-portal price. MariTide (monthly, approved Jul 2031) lists at $1,299 per monthly dose, with an Amgen direct cash price of $549. ≈1.3M users by end 2032, ~80% commercial. 'Metabolic healthspan' and 'focus' wellness users ≈4.5M: ≈2.6M in cash/direct telehealth memberships ($199–349) and ≈1.9M in gray. The gray market is mostly imported generic pens ($6–40 plus shipping, now including generic tirzepatide), 503A 'personalised' compounded semaglutide ($119–229) and research-use retatrutide ($90–200). CBP and FDA estimate 1 in 6 mail-intercepted 'semaglutide' units is mislabelled, underdosed, insulin-substituted or non-sterile.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide, Jul 2031)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, Apr 2032, with hepatic monitoring)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic healthspan' memberships for normal-BMI adults: low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo plus CGM, DEXA and strength coaching, now offered by the largest telehealth platforms and concierge chains
monthly MariTide 'maintenance' dosing every 6–8 weeks among affluent former weekly users
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
research-peptide retatrutide in gyms; imported generic tirzepatide pens by mail
gambling and compulsive-shopping reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The monthly driver is realised by Amgen's MariTide. Its BLA was filed Jul 2030, it was approved Jul 2031 after standard review, and it launched under supply limits. Its label carries a long-washout caution: effects persist roughly 6–10 weeks after the last dose, which matters for perioperative holds and for adverse events. There is still no implant. Survodutide was resubmitted and approved in Apr 2032 with hepatic monitoring; launch is small and it is priced at tirzepatide parity. Amycretin's resubmission is still pending because Novo's North Carolina site cleared reinspection only in mid-2032; a decision is expected in 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing. The incretin market is ≈$150B in 2032. US volume grew ~15%, net prices are flat under the stalled price path and the tariff, and ex-US generic erosion deepened. The Paragraph IV settlements push the US semaglutide cliff to Apr 2033 at the earliest.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. The first MariTide dose produces front-loaded nausea and vomiting, and the monthly half-life means symptoms cannot be stopped by skipping a dose. Rates remain highest among imported-pen users dosing without titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. MariTide label recommends dose-escalation and antiemetic guidance.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Persistence after discontinuation remains disputed. MDL 3094 passed ~61,000 filed and tolled claims. The second and third bellwethers (2031) were split: one defence verdict, one plaintiff verdict with a reduced award.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label. Global settlement talks were court-ordered in 2032 and are unresolved. Reserves are rising.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss. Absolute numbers keep rising with retatrutide and imported tirzepatide.
Long-term data still show no causal confirmation. About 9,000 pancreatitis claims are in the MDL, and settlement modelling prices them regardless.
Remains a population problem in 65+ on unmonitored low-efficacy regimens. It is newly seen in normal-BMI wellness users who lose lean mass from an already lean baseline.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The 2028 class label update stands. Bridge counselling is retained. There is still no HRSA body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. The first pediatric registry interim (2032, n≈4,100) shows lower-than-expected BMD z-score gain in adolescents (−0.2 SD) that the investigators call 'not interpretable' without a matched comparator.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA is recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. FDA asked for an expanded comparator arm; no pediatric label change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association. The anhedonia labelling explicitly distinguishes reduced pleasure from suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / anhedonia (reduced pleasure, emotional flattening)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The retatrutide postmarketing study (2031, validated SHAPS/DARS scales, 72 weeks) found clinically meaningful anhedonia in 7.6% on the top dose vs 2.3% on placebo. Pooled semaglutide and tirzepatide reanalyses give ~4–5% vs ~2% at maintenance doses. Effects are dose-dependent and mostly reversible within 8–12 weeks of stopping, and longer on MariTide. Self-report surveys still find 10–15% of users noticing reduced pleasure.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class labelling (Nov 2031) lists 'anhedonia / reduced interest or pleasure' under Adverse Reactions with trial frequencies and adds a counselling statement. It is not a boxed warning. The FTC continues warning letters, but wellness brands now cite the label in ads; FDA says off-label promotion by non-manufacturers is outside its authority.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Structural stops continue: the 90-day cessation caps, waiver lockouts and HRSA waitlists. On MariTide, regain is slower but follows the same course.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency persist in older and low-income users and appear in normal-BMI wellness users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult follow-up and nine years of adolescent follow-up. About 130k children aged 6–11; pubertal-timing data are still pending.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements and pediatric registry continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: CDC investigated two clusters (2031–32). Insulin-substituted counterfeit pens caused 212 severe hypoglycaemia hospitalisations and 7 deaths. Non-sterile imported pens caused Burkholderia and Serratia bloodstream and injection-site infections: 340 cases in 23 states and 6 deaths. Incretin poison-centre calls rose a further ~60% from 2030.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Alert Network advisory, FDA import alerts, expanded CBP mail seizures and DOJ indictments of two distributor networks, all under existing authority. There is still no prosecution of individual buyers and no new statute.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; more often reported with research-peptide product.
Pharmacodynamic effects persist 6–10 weeks after the last dose. Anaesthesiologists report aspiration-precaution cancellations, and adverse effects cannot be withdrawn quickly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled washout caution. ASA perioperative guidance updated (2032) to a 'treat as full stomach' default.

safety_ledger.effect: Undernutrition, menstrual disruption and eating-disorder masking in normal-BMI users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case series from adolescent-medicine and eating-disorder clinics describe young women on wellness subscriptions with BMI below 18.5 and amenorrhoea. Telehealth screening is inconsistent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Academy for Eating Disorders advisory (2032). The FTC and state medical boards are reviewing two platforms; no FDA action.

food_and_beverage.state: With one adult in five on the drug and 4.5M lean people dosing for 'healthspan', volume losses in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks continue at about the 2028–30 rate, not faster. Majors finish divesting indulgent brands to private-equity owners who target non-users and the bottom third. Protein, fibre, creatine and 'bone-support' formats are now mainstream shelf categories. The split basket by zip code persists.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes fall a third consecutive cycle as AUD coverage reaches heavy drinkers and wellness users drink less. Premium single-serve, low-ABV and non-alcoholic lines take shelf share. Tobacco excise receipts undershoot state forecasts again.

restaurants.state: Fine dining, tasting menus and protein-forward fast casual are steady. Value-volume chains keep closing suburban units, and buffets are a shrinking niche. Alcohol attach rates fall further; 'half-portion' pricing is standard at mid-market chains.

apparel.state: Athletic-cut tailoring is the profitable segment; plus-size keeps shrinking. Resale platforms move record volumes of clothing people grew out of in both directions.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios bundle 'healthspan' prescriptions through partner telehealth. Low-cost gyms keep gaining. Gym-floor research peptides draw DOJ attention after the counterfeit clusters.

insurance.state: No structural change. Pharmacy trend moderates to ~+9% as volume growth slows at flat prices. Employers favour monthly MariTide where they cover weight, for adherence. Some employers quietly drop 'focus' perks after the anhedonia label on counsel's advice; others keep them.

pharma.state: Lilly still leads. Amgen enters with MariTide and is supply-limited. Novo is stabilised but carries the larger MDL exposure. Net prices are flat; volume, not price, drives growth. The Paragraph IV settlements protect 2032 US semaglutide revenue but draw an FTC pay-for-delay inquiry. Indian and Chinese generic makers grow ex-US and, unwillingly, feed the gray market.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Bodies now tell three things: the molecule, the payer and whether the person had a coach. A lean, muscled, DEXA-tracked body, increasingly on monthly MariTide, reads as money and time. A thinner, softer body reads as clinic liraglutide or an imported pen. A heavier body reads as waitlist, lockout, choice or a 90-day gap. A very lean young woman with no muscle reads, in some cities, as a 'healthspan' membership gone too far.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Class stratification is explicit. In Charlotte's banking and fintech workforce, 'the Charlotte build' (men 30–49, retatrutide or MariTide via concierge practice, quarterly DEXA) has been joined by 'the Charlotte finish' among women in client-facing roles. A former analyst's EEOC charge alleges promotion decisions tracked body composition, and recruiters there now say on record that they are trained not to comment on it. Bottom-third use grew only slightly as HRSA flat-funding created waitlists. The low-income marginal user is on imported product, and the counterfeit clusters fell hardest on them.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller meals are the national default. 'Healthspan' households eat protein-weighed plates at fixed times. Family-table negotiations over children on liraglutide are routine in pediatric visits. Weddings serve two menus; holiday dinners in mixed families are planned around dosing day or, for MariTide users, dosing week.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list molecule and cadence ('monthly'). 'Imported' is now a warning, not just a put-down, after the CDC advisories. Partners discuss the anhedonia label the way an earlier generation discussed SSRIs and libido.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is a clinical variable and, for the affluent, a dial set to an optimum. The healthspan framing extends this to people with no excess weight at all: appetite is something even the healthy are expected to manage. A craving left untreated still reads as a choice.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The Nov 2031 class label gives trial anhedonia rates of ~4–5% at maintenance doses and 7.6% at top-dose retatrutide, each against ~2% on placebo. Self-report surveys still find 10–15% of long-term users notice reduced pleasure. About 4.5M adults use low-dose regimens for 'focus', 'calm' or 'healthspan', inside the cash (≈2.6M) and gray (≈1.9M) shares. Brands now advertise the labelled effect directly ('FDA-recognised reward modulation').
interior_life.framing: Labelled side effect and marketed feature at once. The label calls it 'anhedonia / reduced interest or pleasure'. Brands call it 'quiet', clinicians 'reward modulation', users who dislike it 'the grey'. AUD and cessation prescribers call it the mechanism.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Finance, call-centre and logistics employers that subsidise 'focus' memberships split after the label: some keep the perk with a signed counselling acknowledgement, and some end it to limit liability. Union contract language barring employer access to adherence data spreads to two more national agreements. Monthly dosing ends the 'off-dose before the pitch' habit for MariTide users, and sales staff who want that option stay on weekly agents.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' work is a marketing category: festivals have unmedicated stages and streaming services tag specials 'recorded off'. Short, intense leisure (sauna, cold plunge, single tastings) keeps growing. Sports-betting operators again cite softer handle in high-uptake states. A run of novels and one prestige series about 'the grey' receive mixed reviews and strong sales.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists use the label's language in intake. Couples on monthly agents can no longer take dose holidays around anniversaries, and therapists report that as a new complaint. Some report fewer fights and less wanting, and call both true.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The label gave talk radio a citation: 'pacification pills' is now quoted alongside FDA text. A contested political-science preprint claims slightly lower primary turnout in high-uptake precincts; others attribute it to age and income. Candidates are asked whether they are on, and now also whether they are on monthly. No legislation followed.

state.regulatory_posture: Approves new agents with caution: MariTide with a washout caution, survodutide with hepatic monitoring, amycretin still pending. It labelled anhedonia with numbers rather than a boxed warning. Enforcement against counterfeits stays within existing authority: CDC advisories, import alerts, CBP seizures and two DOJ distributor indictments. There is no new statute and no buyer prosecution. FTC polices wellness claims and opened a pay-for-delay inquiry into the semaglutide settlements.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new state action. HRSA is flat-funded at $4.5B by continuing resolutions, the Bridge was extended unchanged, and the ACA cessation mandate and AUD parity still apply. There is no mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, 12-month lockout after two misses). The three pending applications are still pending. Plaintiffs now argue that monthly clinic-administered dosing would satisfy adherence without kiosks; the states have not responded. HRSA sites still require only refill pickup.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea clearance still makes tirzepatide a de facto requirement for some drivers. The Army recruit policy is unchanged. The VA continues semaglutide for AUD and is piloting MariTide in rural clinics under existing formulary authority.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff stands. India's and China's generic expansion, including tirzepatide ex-US, makes US mail imports cheaper and more plentiful. Counterfeit networks traced through Mexico and Southeast Asian fulfilment hubs are now a standing item in bilateral customs talks. Indian API still feeds 503A compounders.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles Paragraph IV litigation with US generic filers, licensing generic semaglutide entry no earlier than April 2033; TrumpRx cash prices stay at $349/$449/$199 and the FTC opens a pay-for-delay inquiry
FDA approves Amgen's MariTide, the first monthly incretin injection, with a long-washout caution; Amgen sets list at $1,299 per dose and direct cash at $549 and rations launch supply

CDC Health Alert Network advisory links insulin-filled counterfeit 'semaglutide' pens and non-sterile imported generic pens to severe hypoglycaemia and bloodstream infections in 23 states; FDA issues import alerts and DOJ indicts two distribution networks

After retatrutide postmarketing data show clinically meaningful anhedonia in 7.6% on top dose versus 2.3% on placebo, FDA adds 'anhedonia / reduced interest or pleasure' with trial frequencies to all incretin labels

Two of the largest US telehealth platforms launch 'metabolic healthspan' memberships for normal-BMI adults, bundling low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo with CGM and DEXA; combined wellness enrolment passes 4 million
A former analyst files an EEOC charge alleging a Charlotte bank's promotion decisions tracked employees' body composition, putting 'the Charlotte build' into a federal filing

open_tensions: The US semaglutide patent cliff is now April 2033 by settlement, under an FTC inquiry. Meanwhile 11M Americans buy cheaper imported generics, some counterfeit, and the gap between legal price and import price keeps widening.

Anhedonia is labelled with a number, yet still advertised as 'focus', subsidised by some employers and used as the treatment mechanism for alcohol and nicotine. No one has decided whether it is a harm, a feature or a liability.
Monthly MariTide makes adherence passive for those who can get it. That undercuts the Indiana and Arkansas weigh-in kiosks and creates a new problem: adverse effects that cannot be stopped for weeks.

HRSA flat funding and waitlists push low-income users toward imported pens just as the counterfeit clusters hit them. The first ambiguous pediatric bone data arrive for ~130k children aged 6–11 on the free generic.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
TrumpRx/direct cash prices remain $349 for semaglutide, $449 for tirzepatide and $199 for oral starting doses, under the Section 232 tariff.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: The Finish: 57 Million on the Drug, a Label That Admits 'the Grey', and a Body That Shows Who Paid
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032, a little over one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, about fifty-seven million people. Growth has slowed. The price did not come down. It did not go up either. In February 2031 Novo Nordisk settled with the generic companies challenging its patents, and the earliest date for a legal American generic semaglutide moved to April 2033. The cash portal still charges $349 for semaglutide, $449 for tirzepatide and $199 for the starter pill. The tariff is still in place, Wegovy still lists at $1,349, and retatrutide is still allocated. The FTC has opened an inquiry into the settlement. Nothing else about who pays has changed. The free federal clinic programme was rolled over at the same $4.5 billion, and its waitlists now run past two months. The Medicare Bridge was extended on the same terms. Insurers still pay for quitting smoking and for drinking less.

Two things are new. The first is a monthly shot. Amgen's MariTide was approved in July 2031, and about 1.3 million people now take it, most of them on commercial plans. Employers like it because adherence is no longer something a person decides each week. Anaesthesiologists like it less, because its effects last up to ten weeks after the last dose, which means surgeries get rescheduled and side effects cannot be stopped quickly. In Indiana, plaintiffs suing over the Medicaid waiver argue that a shot given in a clinic once a month makes the weigh-in kiosk pointless. The state has not answered.

The second is a number. In November 2031 the FDA added anhedonia, reduced interest or pleasure, to every incretin label. The figures are about five percent at maintenance doses and nearly eight percent on top-dose retatrutide, against two percent on placebo. Wellness brands put the label in their advertising. The healthspan memberships sold by the big telehealth platforms now enrol more than four million adults, most of whom were never overweight. For a monthly fee they get a low-dose pill, a glucose sensor and a scan that measures muscle and bone. Some employers stopped paying for 'focus' subscriptions after their lawyers read the label. Others had employees sign a counselling form and kept paying. Eating-disorder clinics have started reporting young women whose membership kept working after they were already too thin.

Cheap product keeps arriving from abroad. India and Brazil now sell generic tirzepatide, and Chinese ingredient supply has doubled. Imported pens cost as little as six dollars a month, and about eleven million Americans buy outside the regulated system. In September 2031 the CDC linked counterfeit pens to two clusters. Some pens contained insulin, which sent people to hospital with blood sugar crashes. Others were non-sterile and caused bloodstream infections. Thirteen people died. Two distribution rings were indicted. No buyer has been charged, and the pens still come by mail.

The bodies show it. In Charlotte the men in banking have their build and the women in client-facing jobs have their finish: concierge prescribing, a monthly injection, a coach, a scan every quarter. In June a former analyst filed a federal discrimination charge saying promotions followed body composition, and recruiters now say on record that they are trained not to notice. Lower down the income scale, use grew slowly. The people who got in recently mostly bought imported pens, and they were the ones who ended up in hospital. About 130,000 children aged six to eleven take free generic liraglutide. The first bone data on them arrived this year and showed a small shortfall that the researchers say cannot yet be interpreted.

Snack makers keep selling off brands, and spirits makers keep cutting guidance. Drugmakers grow on volume, not price. From the outside the country looks calmer, leaner and more sober. A drug label now gives the odds of feeling less, and millions of people pay to take it anyway.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tamika Hollis badges into the fraud-operations floor at 7:52, two floors below the analysts. She swallows her 'focus' tablet with the lukewarm coffee. The bank pays $150 of the $249 membership. In March she signed the form with the FDA paragraph on it, the one with the percentages.

Calls come in. A man in Ohio is crying about his savings. She feels the facts of it and not much else, and she types quickly.

At lunch the elevator fills with men from twenty-six, wide-shouldered and narrow-waisted, holding identical shakers. One of them says 'monthly' like it's a club. She looks at her own reflection in the steel door and decides it's fine.

Her mother texts a photo of a padded envelope with Hindi on the customs slip. Tamika calls her from the stairwell. 'Mama, the news said check the lot number.' 'It's the same lady I always use.' 'The same lady could have a different supplier.' Her mother says the clinic waitlist is nine weeks and she isn't waiting nine weeks to get big again.

At 4:30 the FQHC texts that Jaylen's liraglutide is ready. He's ten. The nurse asks him the questions on the registry form about how he's sleeping and whether he's playing. He says basketball. The nurse writes it down.

Dinner is a rotisserie chicken split three ways, with leftovers. Jaylen talks about a boy whose dad 'gets the shot at the doctor once a month, so he never forgets.'

At ten Tamika sits on the back step. She thinks the evening is nice. She can't tell whether she likes it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Within the 2030 cohort, 10.5 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (56%, up from ~50% because monthly MariTide and clinic-administered dosing lift persistence)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: MariTide covers about 1.3M of 57M users and clinic-administered dosing is barely evidenced, so neither can raise cohort-wide persistence by 6 points. The persistence figure is back-fitted to make the arithmetic close.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In the US, Paragraph IV settlements (Feb 2031) set generic semaglutide entry no earlier than Apr 2033.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism/driver fidelity: the starting world puts US exclusivity at ~2031–32, so an entry date in 2033 is later than expiry. Settlements normally license entry before expiry, and the candidate gives no secondary patents to explain the later date.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Most of the new entrants are normal-BMI 'metabolic healthspan' users in the top third (top 25→29).
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude/mechanism: about 7M net new users are added, but wellness users total only 4.5M, of whom 1.9M are gray-market and 1.5–2M already existed in 2030. The income-third gains (top +4, middle +2.5, bottom +1.2) also don't support 'most' being top-third wellness entrants.

rationale.badness: Class stratification is explicit: the Charlotte build and finish, the EEOC charge, and low-income users pushed onto imported pens that hit them hardest in the counterfeit clusters. Harms also include 13 deaths from counterfeits, eating-disorder masking in lean young women, ambiguous bone data for 130k children, and anhedonia sold as a feature. It is a recognisably harder society, but not structurally hidden, because the anhedonia label is a measured, nameable harm, which lowers the epistemic score.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events (MariTide, anhedonia label, healthspan memberships, counterfeit clusters, stalled price, no new state action, marketed feature). The only strain is the settlement date, which runs later than the parent's stated exclusivity. mechanism: most changes have shown chains, but the persistence rise attributed to MariTide, the 'most new entrants are top-third wellness users' line, and the 2033 settlement date are asserted or conflict with the parent (claims 1–3). magnitude: all headline figures are inside the envelope (21.4% on, 30.5% ever, income thirds and age bands reconcile, payer mix sums to 57.4M, Bridge, Medicaid and HRSA dollars multiply out, MariTide approval exactly 12 months after filing).
